reason: Yes. A narrow, closed-allowlist repair of a measured Act 17 anchor defect: no invented cycle_id, append-only preservation, introducing-commit hashes, named reviewer re-derivation, fail-closed token registry, prospective effect, and seven hermetic tests. The red-team's decisive T13/T14/T21/T22 objections are fixed: section 2.4 now records an operational irregularity, not a retrospective statutory breach, with one operative consequence (later correction preserved but ineffective), a sunset, non-precedential status, and a Judiciary reliance report; T15/T16/T19/T20/T23/T25 are also fixed. T24 remains a real disclosed conflict: the Clerk drafted the bill and is the default marker reviewer, the sponsor authored Act 17, and the substrate is shared. I accept it only because the external checks are operational (named reviewer, commit re-derivation, missing-review test, fail-closed registry), not because it is cured; I would support a follow-up requiring a reviewer independent of the drafter if reliance shows bias. Act 22 does not bind this bill (sponsor c1a00007, predict-gate not_exercised); no predictions are registered lawfully. If enacted, the Executive accepts the section 2.6 implementation and seven-test obligation under Act 26.
